subject: Stratagem: request for elevated uptime and lower p95 — evaluation and roadmap tradeoffs
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom@stratagem.io>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stratagem.io
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: 99.99% uptime + p95 <100ms for Q3 rollout

Ben —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We’re moving fast and need visibility on two commercial/operational asks before we sign:

1) Can Redwood commit to a 99.99% uptime SLA for our production environment (US region) for the initial 12-month term?
2) We need a guaranteed p95 inference latency under 100ms for our conversational endpoints (typical prompt sizes ~150 tokens). If that’s not possible, what compensating credits or fallback options do you offer?

These are redlines from our platform team and procurement. I attached the formal request doc with our target dates.

If you can’t commit to the numbers in full, please propose the minimal set of contractual concessions and the operational changes required (e.g., dedicated pool, reserved capacity, prioritized routing, etc.). We’re targeting a May 1 launch.

—Tom
Tom Reyes
Head of Platform, Stratagem AI
Tom.Reyes@stratagem.io
+1 415 555 0119

Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: 99.99% uptime + p95 <100ms for Q3 rollout

Forwarding Tom's ask — they want 99.99% uptime + p95 <100ms for a May 1 launch. Procurement wants this in the contract.

Quick summary of constraints from my side:
- They’re a mid-size AI platform, high traffic during daytime windows.
- Likely >500 RPS at peak; prompts average 150 tokens.
- Willing to pay for reserved capacity but procurement will push back on high recurring fees.

Questions for product/infra:
1) At present, what is our realistic p95 for a pinned model on a dedicated pool for 150-token prompts in US region?
2) What engineering changes or mitigations would be necessary to guarantee <100ms p95 (e.g., micro-batching limits, kernel config, lower-max-context)? Rough ETA and one-time effort estimate please.
3) If we cannot meet both numbers, what set of contractual concessions (service credit schedule / outage credit, fallbacks such as prioritized routing to dedicated nodes, or allowed maintenance windows) would be acceptable from your perspective?

I’ve attached the Stratagem PDF. We need a response to the customer by EOD Mon so procurement has time to assess.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 99.99% uptime + p95 <100ms for Q3 rollout

Ben —

Quick take after syncing with serving-runtime and infra:

Short answer: we can't confidently promise 99.99% + p95 <100ms for arbitrary peak load without dedicated commitments and operational changes. But there are structured paths we can offer.

Options (ordered by technical feasibility / cost):

A) Reserved Dedicated Pool + Pre-warm + Strict QoS (recommended):
- Provision a dedicated reserved pool sized for Stratagem's peak (we estimate 30–40 A100-equivalent GPU capacity for their stated peak).
- Enable pre-warming and strict priority queuing for their API keys.
- Expected p95: ~70–120ms depending on prompt variability; variability edge cases at burst can push above 100ms unless we tighten batching.
- Uptime: with dedicated fleet + active-standby across two AZs, realistic contractual commitment: 99.98% (requires runbook and on-call escalation guarantees).
- Tradeoffs: high committed monthly cost; ~2–3 week provisioning lead time; ops runbook required.

B) Hybrid: Dedicated baseline + Shared burst with fallback credits
- Dedicated pool sized for base load (70–80% of usual traffic) + shared pool for spikes.
- We can offer a contractual p95 target for the dedicated pool only; for spillover to shared pool we define a credit schedule.
- This lowers cost but complicates SLA language.

C) Hosted with aggressive engine tuning (no dedicated pool)
- For non-dedicated customers we can tune kernels, lower max tokens, and apply KV-prefix caching to improve p95. Still, guaranteeing <100ms p95 across all traffic is high risk.

What we need from sales/procurement to proceed:
- Confirmation whether customer will accept a dedicated reserved commitment (monthly).
- Acceptance of a two-tiered SLA (dedicated pool guarantee + credit schedule for shared spill).
- Approval for a one-time provisioning and runbook creation effort (estimated 120 engineer-hours across runtime/infra/sre).

I attached a short prod-impact matrix and a draft runbook excerpt (prod-impact-matrix.xlsx, runbook-downtime-fallback.txt).

If you want, we can scope a 30-minute triage call Monday AM to finalize the proposal text for procurement.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: prod-impact-matrix.xlsx, runbook-downtime-fallback.txt
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: 99.99% uptime + p95 <100ms for Q3 rollout

Team —

We need to treat this as a priority escalation. Stratagem is in active procurement and fast-moving. A couple of commercial notes from sales leadership:
- We can accept a two-tier SLA: guaranteed p95 and uptime for a dedicated pool + defined credits for spillover, but finance needs a capped exposure on credits.
- I propose the following commercial package to offer Tom by EOD Monday:
  1) Dedicated reserved pool sized for base load (estimated cost $X/month — placeholder until infra provides exact number).
  2) Target SLA: 99.98% uptime on dedicated pool; p95 target <100ms for requests served by that pool.
  3) Spillover policy: if requests are routed to shared pool (more than 5% of total monthly requests), customer receives a 5% service credit for the month for each additional 5% spill, capped at 20%.
  4) One-time engineering provisioning fee (covers runbook and capacity setup).

Ask to product/infra: can you commit to deliver a final capacity estimate and the engineer-hours estimate by Monday 10am PT? Finance will then finalize the credit exposure numbers.

If we can get those numbers we’ll finalize contract language and route to Sarah in Legal for a narrow SLA amendment.

—Karthik
VP, Strategic Accounts (acting)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: 99.99% uptime + p95 <100ms for Q3 rollout — proposed path forward

Tom —

Thanks for the clear ask and the doc. Quick recap and our proposed path forward so procurement has something concrete to review:

1) We are able to offer a dedicated reserved pool with an elevated SLA for that pool. Technical team estimates the baseline configuration will deliver p95 in the ~70–120ms window depending on prompt variability; with additional tuning and guardrails we can get reliably under 100ms for the majority of traffic.

2) Commercially we propose:
   • Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commitment) — capacity to be finalized by Monday 10am PT (we’ll share the exact GPU counts and cost).
   • SLA: 99.98% uptime for the dedicated pool.
   • p95 target <100ms for requests served by dedicated pool.
   • Spillover policy: credit schedule if >5% of monthly requests are served from shared capacity (details in the attached doc). Cap on credits to limit finance exposure.
   • One-time provisioning fee to cover runbook creation & pre-warm.

Next steps:
- Laura’s team will confirm capacity and an engineering-hours estimate by Monday 10am PT.
- I’ll share a short contract appendix draft that encodes the SLA + spillover credit schedule.
- If the numbers are acceptable, we propose a 30-minute call Tuesday to walk procurement/legal through the appendix.

Appended below is the snippet of Laura's note for reference.

Regards —
Ben Carter
